The burst was detected by the **ECLAIRs** onboard trigger (**et875**, **sb25110301**), both by the Count-Rate Trigger (CRT) and the Image Trigger (IMT), which produced a sequence of 24 alerts. CRT provided the alert with the best signal-to-noise-ratio in the image (SNR) of 103.94 in the 8-120 keV energy band over a time window of 10.20 seconds starting at **Tb**=2025-11-03T04:46:26 (UT). 
The light curve sent by the trigger in real-time shows a soft precursor (visible in 5-20 keV of about 5 s duration) and a very prominant main peak (visible in 5-120 keV of about 10 s duration).

The **ECLAIRs** photon data were analyszed on ground  (GCN 42781). With respect to the trigger time **T0**=2025-11-03T04:46:26 (UT, defined as the end of the time window of the first alert received on ground), the precursor ranging from T0-4s to T0+2s is best fit by a powerlaw with photon index of -3.01 and an energy fluence of 4.97E-8 erg/cm2 and the main peak ranging from T0+2s to T0+16s is best fit by a broken powerlaw with a photon index of -1.18, an Epeak=122 keV and an energy fluence of 8.33E-6 erg/cm2 [all fluences are integrated in 4-120 keV].

**GRB 251222A** (also associated with **EP251222b** ) was triggered by **SVOM/ECLAIRs** at **2025-12-22T17:05:46** UTC (T0=61031.712337963 is defined as the SVOM trigger) and is a **long GRB** , detected for ** >200 s** in 4–120 keV with multiple peaks (GCN 43516). The burst was independently detected by Fermi/GBM at 2025-12-22 17:05:51.27 UT with **T90 ≈ 83 s** (50–300 keV, GCN 43222). SVOM/GRM triggered at 2025-12-22T17:05:52 UT with **T90 = 85.5 (+3.0/−3.5) s** (15–5000 keV, GCN 43202). Einstein Probe/WXT detected EP251222b with an event starting at 2025-12-22T17:04:52 UT and lasting **~350 s** (0.5–4 keV, GCN 43215). Konus-Wind reported a long burst with total duration **~83 s** and prompt spectral fits (CPL; e.g. time-integrated **Ep ~ 102 keV** ) and derived energetics assuming **z = 3.171** (including **Eiso ≈ 2.21×10^53 erg** ) - GCN 43214. The **X-ray** counterpart was found by **Swift/XRT** (GCN 43191, GCN 43213) at RA, Dec (J2000) = 05:08:46.81, −07:12:48.7. 
A optical follow-up campaign was performed including **SVOM/VT** (GCN 43189,GCN 43203), **NOT** (GCN 43194), **Calapai** (GCN 43195), **DFOT** (GCN 43207, GCN 43224), **LCO** (GCN 43208, GCN 43212), **GOTO** (GCN 43209), **SVOM/COLIBR** (GCN 43225), **ZTSH** (GCN 43226), **KNC** (GCN 43229), **AbAO** (GCN 43230), **FTW** (GCN 43233), **Kinder** (GCN 43236), **NUTTelA-TAO** (GCN 43237), **Mephisto** (GCN 43250), **Mondy** (GCN 43273). The redshift was measured by **VLT/X-shooter** (GCN 43204). Radio observation was performed with **VLA** (GCN 43415).  The coordinates of the Skyportal page of the ones provided by the detection of the afterglow optical counterpart of SVOM/VT. To be confirmed: TAROT, COLIBRI

Swift Burst Alert Telescope (BAT) detected a 5s relatively short-duration GRB at 21-02-2025 03:34:37 UT (T0=60727.14903935 [MJD]) with the position 59.477, -15.139 (uncertainty of 3 arcmin) (GCN 39396). The peak count rate was ~2200 counts/sec (15-350 keV), at ~0 sec after the trigger. REM 60cm robotic telescope at the ESO observatory detected an optical counterpart 70s after T0 (60727.14984954 MJD) in r = 16.5 +/- 0.2 (GCN 39406). Ongoing, the optical afterglow was detected by the following teams in chronological order: DDRAGO (GCN 39397), REM (GCN 39406), GRANDMA/TAROT (GCN 39417), 1.6m Mephisto (GCN 39412), Mondy (GCN 39424), Assy (GCN 39422), NOT (GCN 39413), LCO (GCN 39425), TNOT (GCN 39446). The possible rebrightening to ~20 mag was reported by one team with two instruments (GCN 39426, GCN 39427) at T+1.4 days (60728.54903935 MJD), but was not confirmed by others. A common redshift of z=0.768 was found by VLT/X-shooter at the position of the afterglow trace ~22.5h after T0 (60728.08653935 MJD). However, no clear emission or absorption features are detected. The X-ray burst emission was detected by the Konus-Wind (GCN 39423) at T+4.4 s (60727.14909028 MJD) and X-ray afterglow by EP-FXT (GCN 39491) at T+2.1 days (60729.24903935 MJD) at the enhanced Swift_XRT position (39404). The radio afterglow was detected by VLA at the centre frequency of 10 GHz (X-band), bandwidth of 4 GHz at T+1.95 days (60729.09903935 MJD), and by ATCA (GCN 39501) at the enhanced Swift-XRT (GCN 39404) position at T+2.2 days (60729.34903935 MJD), with no detection at the initial Swift-XRT position (GCN 39396) at T+6 minutes (60727.15320602 MJD). Swift released refined analysis circulars for the XRT and BAT instruments 1-2 days after the initial trigger (T0). The first XRT refined analysis occurred approximately 600s after the burst, while the BAT detection was refined around 18 hours post-trigger (GCN 39414, GCN 39471). The final BAT analysis yielded a T90 duration of 1.80 +/- 0.32 seconds in the 15-350 keV band.
